stories.focus: Applied Generative AI for Knowledge Workers
stories.headline: AI readiness is measured in connected business processes
stories.read_scope: Complete vendor-sponsored research article: SAP and Oxford Economics survey framing, task-level AI use, nine-percent operating-model adaptation figure, process and data integration argument, governance, readiness dimensions and limits of source-reported survey interpretation.
stories.summary: SAP's vendor-sponsored research with Oxford Economics says surveyed organizations use AI across roughly one quarter of business tasks, while nine percent have fundamentally adapted operations around it. The article argues that scaling depends on connecting AI to trusted data, governed processes, approval policies and regulatory context, not merely adding assistants to individual applications.
stories.why_it_matters: Map one end-to-end process before expanding licenses. Identify the governing data, contract, inventory, approval and compliance conditions; establish an owner and measurable outcome; then test whether AI improves the whole workflow without weakening controls or hiding manual exceptions.
stories.image_alt_intent: A fragmented set of task assistants converges into one governed business process map connecting data, contracts, inventory, approvals, compliance, ownership and measurable workflow outcomes.
stories.freshness_reason: Extended fallback is justified because this is the freshest verified primary research in the selection that quantifies the gap between task-level AI use and process-level operating change, and it remains within 168 hours.

stories.headline: Boards need decision-ready evidence for AI risk
stories.read_scope: Complete governance article: ten board questions covering accountability, strategic review, decision-ready risk, regulatory change, supplier assurance, continuous compliance, incident preparation, combined recovery exercises, resilience and remediation evidence.
stories.summary: SAP offers boards ten evidence-oriented questions covering accountability, strategic review, decision-ready risk, regulatory change, third-party assurance, resilience and incident recovery. The framework positions security and compliance as shared business governance rather than a specialist report, asking leaders to request clear decision rights, tested plans, residual-risk views and proof that remediation actions close.
stories.why_it_matters: Convert one AI initiative into a board-ready evidence pack. Name accountable owners, record the security review that shaped the decision, show residual risk and supplier dependencies, and include the latest combined incident, continuity and recovery exercise with unresolved actions.
stories.image_alt_intent: A board evidence pack connects accountable owners, strategic decisions, residual AI risk, supplier dependencies and the latest tested incident and recovery exercise to open remediation actions.
stories.freshness_reason: This 84-hour source is the freshest verified primary board-level security and compliance evidence in the selection, and it remains within the permitted 168-hour extended fallback.
